Issue #66: predeclared captured-matrix diagnostic, 2026-10-08

Question: Does the captured incorrect 28x28 dense solve recur on Intel Xeon
6973P-C under the pinned R-devel/noLD container? If so, does changing only the
numerical backend path on that same host remove this captured failure?

This branch is isolated diagnostic infrastructure. It must not be merged or
treated as release qualification. No packaged source, acceptance threshold,
published archive, manifest, tag or required check is changed. The published
0.4.1 archive hash remains 8261b2d8084a54fa69a4bb3b7ae0caac3eefcc75ba83969d09422d525460e554.

The protocol is fixed before the first push:
- Twelve ubuntu-latest hosted-runner jobs, at most six concurrent. Preserve all
  CPU allocations and outcomes. No adaptive reruns or success-only selection.
- Same pinned noLD image as the failed release-related run, digest
  sha256:4d8aeacfd5130c824ff593cde19e5ffaed96c170ca397837f56163a201e09389.
- Both hash-pinned, already-public synthetic specimens from issue #66.
- Fixed arm order on each machine: original default; forced NEHALEM; reference
  BLAS/LAPACK; restored original default. Threads fixed at one in all arms,
  matching the observed failing run. Each arm gets three fresh R processes.
- Specimen order is binary/ordinal in processes 1 and 3, ordinal/binary in
  process 2, giving both specimens first-solve coverage. Metadata getters run
  only after the first native forward/back pair has been saved.
- Each process executes twenty predetermined repetitions for each specimen,
  first with its stored factor, then with a newly computed Cholesky factor.
- Compare native triangular solves, independent scalar triangular solves,
  hybrid solves, and scalar backward errors. Keep the existing 32*d*eps bound.
  Record intermediate vectors and every new invalid operation.
- Record CPU details, R and native library identities, actual OpenBLAS core
  and threads, runtime mappings and environment. Reject an unverified backend.
- Reference package installation occurs after the first two arms. Restore and
  verify the original library paths and bytes for the final default arm.

Interpretation is bounded:
- Successful workflow execution means the protocol ran, not that all numerical
  operations passed. Inspect results.tsv and the stored invalid steps.
- No affected CPU obtained: the affected-host question remains unanswered.
- Affected CPU obtained but default replay passes: non-reproduction of these
  captured matrices alone does not clear the earlier package-level failure.
- Default fails, alternate passes, restored default fails on the same machine:
  evidence of backend-path dependence for these specimens. This does not prove
  a CPU hardware defect, a particular instruction defect, or noLD causation.
- A matched ordinary-R build would be needed to establish noLD causation.
- Even clean captured-matrix replays do not qualify the full package on an
  alternate backend; that requires the unchanged archive's package tests/check.

Source rationale:
R backsolve/forwardsolve call DTRSM:
https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/backsolve.html
The exact OpenBLAS version accepts NEHALEM; actual dispatch must be verified:
https://github.com/OpenMathLib/OpenBLAS/blob/v0.3.20/driver/others/dynamic.c
Related, different CPU/operation/threading report is hypothesis only:
https://github.com/OpenMathLib/OpenBLAS/issues/5267
